summary: Plan city plots, crop calendars and safer harvests in a five-day urban agriculture course. Review the practical outline and learning outcomes.
lede: Urban agriculture training helps community garden coordinators, small-plot growers and food-programme staff plan safe, workable city food production. It covers assessing plot access and soil information, planning crop schedules, water and compost use, handling fresh produce safely, and comparing bed-level costs and sales.
audienceIntro: This course suits people who plan, support or operate community gardens and small urban growing sites, including those responsible for land access, crop decisions, produce handling or programme delivery.
modules: FAO Urban Agriculture and Food Access
Urban Land Tenure and Plot Screening
Urban Soil Safety and Raised Beds
Codex Food Hygiene for Fresh Produce
Urban Farm Costs and Local Sales
prerequisites: Prior urban agriculture experience is not required. Basic arithmetic and familiarity with everyday planning or record-keeping are useful. Coding is not required. The Excel exercise uses sample scenario data and requires access to Excel on a laptop; no additional software installation is needed.
